newsitem.title: HONG KONG: LME copper seen struggling with $2,300 again.
newsitem.headline: LME copper seen struggling with $2,300 again.

text.p: Hong Kong metal traders said they expect three-month copper to continue to meet stiff resistance at the $2,300 level later on Monday despite the ongoing strike at Chile's Escondida mine.
"Only a few workers are on strike and with that percentage, I don't think copper production will be affected," said one trader at a Chinese firm.

Three-month copper closed the London Metal Exchange (LME) kerb at US$2,288 a tonne, up $28 dollars, on Friday after faltering at the psychological $2,300 barrier. The Escondida news prompted some covering and buying, traders said.
Escondida said on Friday that the industrial action at the copper mine by workers representing 17 percent of the labour force would not hit the company's operations.
Last week's decline in LME copper stocks is expected to continue, with metal purchased earlier by Chinese buyers moving out of stores, they added.

"Basically I know there are sales that have been made into China which are based on warrants...it doesn't actually come off the figures until the material is moved from the warehouse," a senior metals trader said.
"So that means that it's been allocated and sold, but it still hasn't moved out of the warehouse, I think it will do over the next one to two weeks," he said, without specifying volumes.
LME copper stocks have dipped by 7,200 tonnes over the past week, underpinning prices, brokerage Brandeis said in its Friday metals review.
Some Hong Kong traders expect a quiet trading day on the LME with the Jewish Passover holiday keeping a number of key operators away from the market.
Aluminium prices are expected to inch upwards, largely because LME stocks are dropping at a healthy rate.
LME aluminium closed on Friday at $1,554 a tonne.
LME aluminium stocks dropped last week by 12,375 tonnes, and Hong Kong traders said they expected that trend to continue.
"I'm quite bullish on aluminium," said one trader.
